terms.gloss: pretend not to (know, see); hide that one knows
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with quasi and the subjunctive, or the accusative and infinitive
evidence: Plaut. Mil. 4.2.2: dissimulābō, hōs quasi nōn videam (Lewis & Short s.v. dissimulō)
Traupman 106: I’ll pretend I don’t know him, dissimulābō mē eum nōvisse
terms.comment: To hide what is so: dissimulābō mē eum nōvisse is “I’ll hide that I know him”, so “I’ll pretend not to know him”. Its opposite is simulāre, to pretend what is not so.

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with quasi and the subjunctive
evidence: Ter. Eun. 3.2.8: assimulābō quasi nunc exeam, “will pretend to be just going out” (Lewis & Short s.v. quasi)
Traupman 106: I’ll pretend I’m leaving, assimulābō quasi abeam

phrases.english: I’ll pretend I’m just going out.

phrases.latin: sed ita adsimulātōte, quasi ego sim peregrīnus
phrases.english: but make believe that I am a stranger

sources: The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
Lewis & Short: dissimulo · Lewis & Short: assimulo
